S86.08.needs: The browser must already be paired with the Desktop app (AGI Desktop installed and running).
S86.08.note: The extension shows only this browser's Desktop pairing, not a list of several paired phones or browsers. The web app's Account > Linked devices panel (apps/web/features/settings/components/LinkedDevicesPanel.tsx, text Linked devices, with an Unlink button) lists the Chrome extension and desktop app as linked devices, but that is in the web app, not the Chrome app.
steps: Open the extension's Options page (the page the extension opens with Options; its sections are Permissions, Shortcuts, Options, Account, Help).
Scroll to the section titled Desktop app.
If this browser is paired with Desktop, the Unpair button is visible. Click Unpair.
Read the question that appears: Unpair the desktop app? Browser actions that run through Desktop stop working until you pair again. Click Keep paired to cancel, or Unpair to confirm.
Compare with Expected: the paired device is visible here and Unpair removes the pairing.
S86.08.where: Extension Options page > Desktop app > Unpair (then Unpair again in the question that appears)

S86.09.needs: A signed-in AGI account in the Chrome extension. Use a test account, because the tester is signed out afterwards.
S86.09.note: The side panel's More menu also has a Log out item (apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json, message Log out, shown when the account block is visible); the tester may use either path.
steps: Sign in to the AGI account in the extension.
Open the extension's Options page and click the Account section.
Find the row with the Log out button and read its hint: Remove your AGI account session and saved autofill profile from this device.
Click Log out. The button shows Logging out… while it runs.
Compare with Expected: the account row changes to a signed-out state and the status message appears if the web session or autofill profile could not be removed.
S86.09.where: Extension Options page > Account > Log out

labels.text: Approve a site so the assistant can act on it, and remove it any time.

S86.17.needs: A normal website open in Chrome (not a Chrome settings page).
S86.17.note: The Blocked sites section (apps/extension/src/features/options/blocked-sites-section.ts) is a separate list with its own Remove buttons; blocking a site also removes it from approved sites.
steps: Open a normal website in Chrome, then open the extension's Options page.
Click the Permissions section and find the line Approve a site so the assistant can act on it, and remove it any time.
Click Add next to the current site to approve it. The button changes to Remove.
Open the list of approved sites and click Remove on that site to take it away.
Compare with Expected: the site can be chosen and removed later. Also check the Browser control setting in the same section.
S86.17.where: Extension Options page > Permissions > Add or Remove for the current site (under the line Approve a site so the assistant can act on it, and remove it any time.)

S86.23.note: Searched apps/extension for always allow, always deny, remembered, saved approval and approval in apps/extension/src/features/options/site-permission-policy.ts and apps/extension/src/options.ts. No list of remembered always-allow or always-deny approvals was found. The nearest controls are the approved-sites Add/Remove list (apps/extension/src/options.ts) and Blocked sites (apps/extension/src/features/options/blocked-sites-section.ts); S86.17 covers those.

S86.24.needs: An approved site for the task run. A test site the tester controls is safest.
S86.24.note: The UI labels are Ask first, Auto, Full access and YOLO, not the Expected wording (ask every time, auto-approve safe, autonomous). Auto is the default (apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/askBeforeActing.ts). The side panel drop-down is select id sp-cu-mode-select in apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/computerUsePanel.ts.
steps: Open the extension's Options page and click the Permissions section.
Find the row titled Browser control and open its drop-down.
Choose Ask first, then Auto, then Full access, and read the hint under the row each time.
Start a browser task on an approved site and check that it asks before each action when Ask first is set, and does not ask for routine steps when Auto or Full access is set.
Compare with Expected: the default setting is Auto and the setting is enforced during a run.
S86.24.where: Extension Options page > Permissions > Browser control (drop-down), or the side panel's mode drop-down (labelled with the composer's autonomy text)

S86.26.needs: A web app account with a passkey or security key, and access to the account email. Not available in the Chrome extension.
S86.26.note: The Security settings tab name is taken from the visible text Use Log out of all devices in Security (apps/web/features/settings/sections/AccountSection.tsx line 92); the nav label itself was not confirmed. The hardened behaviour is enforced server-side in apps/web/lib/server/account-security/gate.ts.
steps: In the web app (not the Chrome side panel), open Settings and open the Security section.
Find the Advanced Account Security panel and read its text.
Click Turn on Advanced Account Security, then enter the code from the email.
Read the confirmation: Advanced Account Security is on, with a link that turns it off for the next 48 hours.
Compare with Expected: sign-in is tightened, and every signed-in session needs a passkey or security key check.
S86.26.where: Web app Settings > Security > Advanced Account Security > Turn on Advanced Account Security
